body.estimand_functional: \[R_2(G_n)\asymp r_{\log}(n,d_n),\qquad r_{\log}(n,d)=\frac{d^2}{n\log(d+1)},\] with the upper edge attained by the total graph-dependent procedure \(\mathsf{Compile}(G_n)\) and the lower edge taken over every outcome-independent assignment law and every measurable, possibly randomized estimator.

sampling_model.design: The simple labeled \(d_n\)-regular graph \(G_n\) is drawn uniformly and fully revealed before the experimenter chooses one graph-measurable assignment law. The total compiler first tests \(d_n^2+1<n\): failure returns the all-treated law immediately, while success permits it to evaluate the candidate law that draws \(k_{n,d_n}\) uniform seeds with replacement and treats the union of their closed neighborhoods.
sampling_model.units: Conditional on the revealed graph, the population \(V_n\) and the complete potential-outcome schedule \(y\) are fixed. The schedule may depend on \(G_n\).
sampling_model.treatment: One binary assignment \(Z\) is drawn. The observed data are exactly \(G_n,Z,Y\), where \(Y_i=y_i(Z)\); estimator randomization \(U\) is independent and included in risk.
sampling_model.overlap: No Bernoulli overlap condition is imposed. On the seed branch, the inverse probability \(\pi_i^{(0)}\) is formed only when \(d_n^2+1<n\), which makes it positive; every other finite case uses the all-treated fallback.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no nuisance regressions or prior outcomes. Intermediate-exposure outcomes are unrestricted and ignored.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Corollary 5.4 gives \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\) with high probability for uniform random \(d\)-regular graphs when \(d=o(\sqrt n)\).
Theorem 4.1 bounds the modified Horvitz--Thompson variance by a universal constant times \(\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) times the endpoint empirical second moments.
Theorem 4.8 gives a polynomial exposure-variance guarantee for randomized one-hop-max clustering under restricted growth and bounded outcomes.
Theorem 1.1 gives \(O(\sqrt d)\) control of the nontrivial adjacency spectrum for uniform simple regular graphs through \(d=O(n^{2/3})\).
The main graph-matrix theorems bound norms of fixed polynomial shapes under the uniform random-regular law by switching trace moments.
Corollary 1 proves a spectral-gap result for Boolean graph powering in a sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi regime under a small-radius condition.
The paper proves that the independence number is asymptotic to \(2n\log d/d\) for its growing-degree uniform random-regular regime.
The paper gives necessary and sufficient conditions for unbiasedness and consistency of its design-based Riesz estimator class.

body.tldr: The full matched minimax frontier is not established in this round. The inherited unrestricted lower edge, seed upper certificate, finite compiler, sparse Boolean operator theorem, and dense Boolean-polynomial truncation remain valid. The newly prescribed collision-discrepancy route fails at its sole new premise: an explicit admissible sequence of disjoint projective-plane incidence graphs disproves the proposed graphwise conditional two-switch variance bound. This does not refute the desired high-probability Boolean operator theorem for a uniform random regular graph, but it means that a typical-graph refinement or a genuinely different concentration argument is still required. Consequently the archived logarithmic risk bracket, not \(R_2(G_n)\asymp d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\), remains the unconditional conclusion.

project_justification.gap: Kandiros--Harshaw--S\'{a}vje, Corollary 5.4, leaves the identical \(q=2\) GATE game between \(d_n/n\) and \(d_n^2/n\). The inherited work improves the all-procedure lower edge to \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) and gives a seed-design upper certificate of order \(d_n^2/n\), but the logarithmic gap remains because the dense full right-projected Boolean operator event is unproved.
project_justification.niche: The unchanged field-tier opportunity is to determine whether typical uniform random-regular radius-two geometry permits the inherited outcome-blind seed procedure, or another explicit procedure, to attain the all-procedure lower scale under the exact endpoint-second-moment class.
project_justification.fill: This round stress-tests the proposed collision-discrepancy proof rather than assuming its variance certificate. A projective-plane incidence construction shows that the requested graphwise conditional two-switch estimate is false even along a deterministic dense sequence satisfying \(d_n\to\infty\) and \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\). The target may still be closed by proving an analogous estimate only on a high-probability random-regular event and bounding the exceptional set, or by replacing this concentration spine.

body.related_work: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax remains the theorem-level comparator for the exact decision problem and supplies the published \(d_n/n\)-to-\(d_n^2/n\) bracket. The inherited balanced converse, seed/Rao--Blackwell construction, and finite compiler narrow but do not close that bracket. CookGoldsteinJohnson2018 controls the ordinary adjacency spectrum on the uniform simple regular law, not Boolean radius-two collision discrepancy. Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices does not furnish the previously attempted cancellation-preserving growing-Charlier estimate or its row-sum component. The present two-switch audit adds a different obstruction: the proposed graphwise conditional variance bound itself fails on an explicit regular-graph family, so a valid switching proof must first restrict to and certify a typical graph event. AbbeBoixRalliSandon2020, KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, and UganderYin2023RGCR do not supply that certificate. KarrerEtAl2021Scale remains the intended application: a proved frontier would be a random-regular precision benchmark, not a claim about the platform graph itself.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The dense completion-switching factorial estimate and Boolean-to-polynomial Frobenius remainder remain proved. The new collision-discrepancy route fails before concentration: for a disjoint union of \(m=\lfloor q^{1/3}\rfloor\) incidence graphs of \(\operatorname{PG}(2,q)\), one has \(E=W-B=0\), yet a proportion at least of order \(1/m\) of valid oriented two-switches creates at least \(8(d-2)\) ordered excess-route entries. Thus the conditional squared increment is at least a constant times \(d^2/m\), while the proposed bound for \(S=T=V_n\) is at most a constant times \(d\). Since \(d/m\to\infty\), no universal graphwise estimate of the requested form holds. These graphs can be rare under the uniform regular law, so the unconditional discrepancy tail and the typical Boolean operator bound remain answer-open.
body.honest_scope: The established content consists of the inherited unrestricted converse, seed-risk theorem, finite exact compiler, sparse Boolean operator theorem, and dense factorial-moment and truncation estimates. This round additionally gives a deterministic counterexample to one proposed graphwise switching certificate; it gives no counterexample to the uniform-random-regular operator theorem or to the minimax frontier. No full dense Boolean operator theorem or matched frontier is claimed. The statistical problem remains one assignment with fixed finite-population schedules, arbitrary closed-neighborhood interference, separate endpoint empirical second moments, and all outcome-blind graph-adaptive laws with all measurable randomized estimators.
